questions.stem: The HIGHEST peak in India is:
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga — on Sikkim-Nepal border, 8,586 m, world's 3rd-highest peak, highest entirely within or on India. K2 is highest in the POK region but claimed by India. Everest is on Nepal-Tibet border, not in India. Nanda Devi (7,816 m) — highest peak wholly within India.

questions.stem: The HIMALAYAN range is divided into THREE parallel ranges. Match: A. Greater Himalayas.  B. Lesser Himalayas (Himachal).  C. Outer Himalayas. List-II: 1. Himadri.  2. Pir Panjal + Dhauladhar.  3. Shivalik.
questions.explanation: Three ranges N to S: (1) Himadri / Greater Himalayas — tallest, incl. Everest, Kangchenjunga, Nanda Devi. (2) Himachal / Lesser Himalayas — Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mussoorie, Mahabharat ranges; hill stations Shimla, Darjeeling, Nainital. (3) Shivalik / Outer — foothills.

questions.stem: India's COASTLINE total length is approximately:
questions.explanation: Total coastline ~7,500 km including Andaman & Nicobar Islands + Lakshadweep. Mainland coast: ~6,100 km. Coastal states (west to east): Gujarat (LONGEST), Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal. including island territories.

questions.stem: The DECCAN PLATEAU is bounded on the WEST by:
questions.explanation: Deccan Plateau — bounded by Western Ghats (W), Eastern Ghats (E), Satpura + Vindhya (N), Kanyakumari (S). W. Ghats are taller (~1,500-2,695 m; Anamudi highest). E. Ghats — lower, discontinuous (cut by rivers). Plateau itself was formed by Deccan Traps (flood basalts, Cretaceous era).

questions.stem: The highest peak of the WESTERN GHATS is:
questions.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) — Kerala, highest in peninsular India. Nilgiri Doddabetta (2,637 m) is in TN. Mahendragiri (1,501 m) — highest of the Eastern Ghats. Nanda Devi is in Himalayas (Uttarakhand). W. Ghats UNESCO WHS since 2012. 2,695 m, Kerala.

questions.stem: The ARAVALLI range is located in:
questions.explanation: Aravalli — oldest fold mountain range in India, extending NE-SW from Delhi through Haryana and Rajasthan. Length ~692 km. Highest peak Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) at Mt Abu. Heavily eroded over billion-plus years. Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi.

questions.stem: The COLDEST inhabited place in India is traditionally:
questions.explanation: Dras (Ladakh UT) — one of the coldest inhabited places in the world. Recorded temperatures as low as −60 °C (though typical min is around −22 °C). Population around 1,500. Also strategically important — Kargil battle key location. called 'Gateway to Ladakh'; Kargil district, Ladakh.

questions.stem: Majuli, recognised as one of the world's largest inhabited river islands, is situated in which Indian river?

options.option_text: Ganga River near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh
Godavari River in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
Mahanadi River in Chhattisgarh or Odisha

questions.explanation: Majuli in Assam is formed by the Brahmaputra and its distributaries and is a UNESCO-nominated cultural landscape. The Ganga, Godavari, and Mahanadi do not form a comparable large inhabited mid-river island. A common distractor is Godavari because it also has islands, but none rivals Majuli's scale.

questions.stem: Which mountain system serves as the traditional geographical dividing line between the Indo-Gangetic Plains to the north and the Peninsular block to the south?

options.option_text: Eastern Ghats running along the eastern coast
Vindhya-Satpura ranges stretching east to west
Chota Nagpur Plateau in eastern India

questions.explanation: The Vindhya Range (and the parallel Satpura) runs roughly east–west and marks the conventional physical boundary between the northern plains and peninsular India. The Aravallis, while old, run diagonally through Rajasthan and do not separate the Peninsula from the plains; the Eastern Ghats and Chota Nagpur lie entirely within the peninsula.

questions.stem: The Palghat Gap is a critically important low-elevation corridor in the Western Ghats. Which two states does it connect?

options.option_text: Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh via the Deccan plateau
Kerala and Tamil Nadu through the Palakkad district
Goa and Karnataka through the Sahyadri foothills
Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh near the Nilgiri Hills

questions.explanation: The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap is about 30 km wide and links Palakkad in Kerala with Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu. It is the only major break in the otherwise continuous Western Ghats south of the Nilgiris, making it strategically important for railways and roads. Karnataka–AP and Goa–Karnataka are tempting because both states share the Ghats, but this gap lies further south.

questions.stem: In the Himalayan foothills, underground streams disappear into the porous Bhabar zone and reappear further south as springs and swampy land. This re-emergence zone is called:

options.option_text: Duars — flat alluvial grassland belt of Assam region
Khadar — fresh alluvial soil of active river floodplains
Bhangar — older alluvial deposit on raised river terraces
Terai — marshy, swampy tract where underground streams resurface

questions.explanation: The Terai lies immediately south of the Bhabar belt; streams that sank into coarse boulders of Bhabar reappear here, creating a waterlogged, forested zone. Duars is the equivalent term for Assam/West Bengal wet grasslands — a frequent mix-up. Khadar and Bhangar describe alluvial soil types of the plains, not foothill sub-zones.

questions.stem: The Loktak Lake, famous for its floating masses of soil and vegetation called 'phumdis', is the largest freshwater lake in which part of India?

options.option_text: Northeast India — located in Manipur state
Eastern India — located in Odisha state
Southern India — located in Karnataka state
Central India — located in Madhya Pradesh state

questions.explanation: Loktak Lake in Manipur is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India; the Keibul Lamjao National Park — the world's only floating national park — rests on its phumdis. Odisha's Chilika is a well-known large lake but it is a saltwater coastal lagoon, not a freshwater lake, making it the most tempting wrong answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following mountain passes is correctly matched with the Indian state in which it actually lies?

options.option_text: Nathu La — Sikkim, connecting to Tibet (China)
Zoji La — Himachal Pradesh, on the Manali–Leh axis
Rohtang Pass — Uttarakhand, on the Tibet trade route
Lipu Lekh — Jammu & Kashmir, Kailash Mansarovar route

questions.explanation: Nathu La (≈4,310 m) in Sikkim is a key India–China trade pass reopened in 2006 — correctly matched. Zoji La lies in Ladakh (J&K), not Himachal Pradesh. Rohtang Pass is in Himachal Pradesh (Kullu–Lahaul corridor), not Uttarakhand. Lipu Lekh is in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand — not J&K. Examiners frequently swap states across these four passes.

questions.stem: The Shillong Plateau is geologically described as an 'outlier of the Peninsular Shield' rather than part of the Himalayan system. Which statement correctly explains this classification?

options.option_text: It formed from Tertiary marine sediment, unlike the crystalline Himalayan ranges
Its Pre-Cambrian crystalline rocks match the Peninsular Shield, not Himalayan folds
It is a detached block fully isolated by the Brahmaputra floodplain on all sides
It formed by the same basaltic lava eruptions that produced the Deccan Traps

questions.explanation: The Shillong Plateau consists of ancient Pre-Cambrian gneisses and granites — the same hard crystalline rock type that forms the Deccan/Peninsular Shield. The Himalayas, by contrast, are young Tertiary fold mountains built from sedimentary uplift. Option C is geographically partly true (Brahmaputra separates it spatially) but does not explain the geological kinship with the Peninsula. Option D confuses it with the Deccan Trap basalts, which are igneous extrusive rocks of a completely different origin.
